scope.summary: Implement the machine-readable export validation report per Section 13.26 (GREQ-035): a per-target checklist (influence caps, blendshape counts, bone counts, material counts, texture sizes, LODs, unit/axis checks) emitted as a typed artifact that the EXPORT_BODY_VALID descriptor consumes and that blocks promotion of failing exports.
acceptance_criteria: The report schema (versioned, schemars-published) covers per-check entries: check id, measured value, allowed budget, PASS/FAIL/WARN, and remediation hint; every export emits one report per target.

Checks include at minimum: influence cap compliance, blendshape count vs budget (GREQ-012 lint thresholds), bone count, material count, texture sizes vs platform preset, LOD presence/counts, unit/axis contract verification, and lane-specific caveats (UE glTF morph bug advisory).
EXPORT_BODY_VALID evaluates the report mechanically; any FAIL blocks the export artifact from promotion (PromotionGate integration) while WARN promotes with the warning attached.
Reports are addressable from the export_body MCP result and persisted alongside the manifest for audit.
scope.risk_if_missed: Export quality becomes human-eyeball-only: agents and CI cannot gate on export health, and broken exports promote silently until a Blender/UE user finds them days later.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Emits/extends the TAILOR_BODY_* KernelEventType family on the EventLedger per Section 13.16 (extends the 13.14 canonical list).
internal_diagnostics ships with WP-KERNEL-012; wire the open diagnostic-event API for this behavior in the WP-KERNEL-016 retrofit.
Palmistry external watcher ships with WP-KERNEL-012/016; long generation/bake/export runs get child-stall watch coverage in the retrofit.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.
